challenges.title: Draw the closest object to you
challenges.description: Look at the closest object within reach, and draw it exactly as it is in 10 minutes.
tips: Start with the big shapes: a rectangle, a circle, before any detail.
Look at the object more often than at your paper, that's where the likeness happens.
Wobbly lines are what give a sketch its charm, don't erase them.

challenges.title: Self-portrait from behind
challenges.description: Draw yourself from behind, or from memory, without looking in a mirror.
tips: Focus on the silhouette: shoulders, neck and hair are enough to recognise you.
From behind there's no face to get right, which is what makes this one approachable.
A photo taken over your shoulder works as a reference if memory fails you.

challenges.title: Your hand holding an object
challenges.description: Pick an everyday object, hold it, and draw your hand holding it.
tips: Hold your hand still for a few seconds and study it before drawing anything.
Draw the object first, then the fingers around it, it's easier in that order.
If a whole hand feels daunting, crop in tight on two or three fingers.

challenges.title: One-minute sketch through the window
challenges.description: Look through the nearest window and sketch what you see in 5 minutes flat.
tips: Five minutes is short: aim for the overall impression, not accuracy.
Lay down the horizon or a building edge first, everything else falls into place.
Skip distant details, a few strokes are enough to suggest them.

challenges.title: Your meal before you eat it
challenges.description: Before your next meal or snack, take two minutes to sketch it.
tips: Sketch fast, before it gets cold, that's part of the game.
Plates and glasses are ellipses, never perfect circles.
A simple outline is enough, you can ignore colour entirely.

challenges.title: A texture around you
challenges.description: Find an interesting texture nearby (fabric, wood, wall) and draw it in detail.
tips: Pick a small square of the surface rather than the whole texture.
Vary your pencil pressure to suggest depth.
Repeat the pattern without chasing perfect regularity, the eye fills in the rest.

challenges.title: An animal from memory
challenges.description: Draw an animal of your choice purely from memory, without looking at a reference.
tips: Start with the overall body shape, then add the head and legs.
It won't look much like the animal, and that's exactly the point.
Pick an animal you like, you'll have more images in your head.

challenges.title: A shadow
challenges.description: Spot a cast shadow (yours or an object's) and draw its shape.
tips: Draw only the outline of the shadow, like a dark puddle.
Shadows move with the light: take a photo if you want to take your time.
Fill the inside with one flat tone, no gradient.

challenges.title: A plant you saw today
challenges.description: Draw a plant or flower you come across today, in person or in a photo.
tips: Start with the stem, the leaves attach to it naturally afterwards.
No need to draw every leaf, three or four will do.
Notice how the leaves overlap, that's what creates depth.

challenges.title: A room in 10 lines
challenges.description: Draw a room in your home using no more than 10 lines.
tips: Count your strokes out loud, it forces you to pick what matters.
A stroke can be long and curved, a line doesn't have to be a short dash.
Start with the structural lines: floor, walls, ceiling.

challenges.title: Your back-to-routine desk
challenges.description: Draw your workspace exactly as it is right now, without tidying it up first.
tips: The mess says something, whatever you do don't tidy up first.
Place the rectangle of the desk first, then the objects on it.
Three or four objects is plenty, you don't have to draw everything.

challenges.title: A morning routine
challenges.description: Draw the first three things you do each morning, in three panels.
tips: Draw your three frames before anything else, it sets the exercise up.
One gesture per panel: the hand on the alarm, the mug, the door.
Stick figures do the job perfectly here.

challenges.title: Your notebook for the month
challenges.description: Draw the imaginary cover of a notebook that would tell the story of your month ahead.
tips: Think title plus one simple image, like a real cover.
The lettering matters as much as the drawing, leave room for it.
This month hasn't happened yet: make it up, you can't get it wrong.

challenges.title: A hybrid object
challenges.description: Pick two real objects and draw the imaginary object born from mixing them.
tips: Pick two very different objects: the contrast makes the mix more interesting.
Start with the general shapes, the details can come after.
Give it a name, it helps decide what it looks like.

challenges.title: With your weaker hand
challenges.description: Draw a simple object using the hand you don't normally use.
tips: Pick an object with simple shapes, this isn't the moment for detail.
The shaky line is part of the result, don't try to fix it.
Try it a second time if you want to compare.

challenges.title: An invented pattern
challenges.description: Invent a small geometric pattern and repeat it until the page is full.
tips: A pattern of three or four shapes is enough, the repetition does the rest.
Change the pattern slightly partway through if you feel like it.
The result doesn't need to be perfectly regular.

challenges.title: Without looking at your page
challenges.description: Pick an object and draw its outline without ever looking at your page, only at the object.
tips: Put your pen down and don't lift it until the end.
The result will be off, that's the point of the exercise.
An object with simple outlines, like a mug or a plant, works well.

challenges.title: A face in shapes
challenges.description: Draw a face using only simple geometric shapes: circles, triangles, rectangles.
tips: It doesn't need to look like anyone, an imaginary face works just fine.
Start with the shape of the face, then place the shapes for the features on top.
Overlap the shapes instead of placing them side by side, it adds depth.

challenges.title: What's in your bag
challenges.description: Empty your bag or your pockets and draw what you find.
tips: Lay the objects out in front of you rather than drawing them inside the bag.
Pick three or four if drawing everything takes too much space.
The most ordinary objects are often the most interesting to draw.

challenges.title: The map of an imaginary place
challenges.description: Draw the map of a place that doesn't exist: an island, a city, a country.
tips: Start with the big shapes: coastlines, roads, borders, before the details.
Name a few spots on your map, it brings the place to life.
No need for accuracy, an imaginary map has no scale to respect.

challenges.title: Your favorite dish, from memory
challenges.description: Draw your favorite dish purely from memory, without looking at a photo or reference.
tips: Close your eyes for a few seconds first to picture it.
Color and texture matter as much as shape.
What you forget while drawing is also part of the result.

challenges.title: A creature born from a stain
challenges.description: Make an ink or paint stain on the page, then turn it into a creature.
tips: Let the stain dry a little before deciding what it will become.
Turn the page in every direction, a shape usually suggests something.
Add just enough to reveal the creature, no more.

challenges.title: The inside of a drawer
challenges.description: Open a random drawer or cupboard and draw what you find inside.
tips: Leave the objects as they're stored, tidy or messy, both work.
Pick a drawer you haven't opened in a while, there are often surprises.
Focus on two or three objects if the drawer is too full.
